notes_list.title: E1 and E2 Elimination
notes_list.basic_overview: E1 elimination is stepwise through a carbocation; E2 is concerted and requires a suitable β-H/C–LG alignment.
notes_list.extra_info_content: E1 competes with SN1 and is favored by carbocation-stabilizing substrates and heat. E2 is favored by strong bases and often by higher temperature.
notes_list.examples: Tertiary halides can undergo E1 in polar protic media; secondary/tertiary substrates with strong base commonly undergo E2.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: E1: ionizing polar protic medium. E2: strong base; solvent and base sterics influence regioselectivity.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: E1: ionization → carbocation → β-deprotonation. E2: base abstracts β-H as leaving group departs and π bond forms.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: E1 rate ≈ k[substrate]; E2 rate = k[substrate][base].
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Integrates mechanism, kinetics, conformation and regioselectivity.
notes_list.common_traps: Zaitsev product is often favored for small bases under thermodynamic control, while bulky bases can favor Hofmann orientation.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
